title: Implement a binary min-heap from scratch in Rust
description: Greenfield Rust task: implement MinHeap<T: Ord> with push, pop (returns Option<T>), peek (returns Option<&T>), len, and is_empty using a Vec-backed binary heap with sift-up and sift-down.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement MinHeap<T: Ord> in src/lib.rs backed by a Vec.

pub struct MinHeap<T: Ord> { data: Vec<T> }

impl<T: Ord> MinHeap<T> {
    pub fn new() -> Self
    pub fn push(&mut self, val: T)       // add element, sift up
    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<T>   // remove min, sift down
    pub fn peek(&self) -> Option<&T>     // return &min without removing
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool

    fn sift_up(&mut self, i: usize)      // swap with parent while smaller
    fn sift_down(&mut self, i: usize)    // swap with smallest child while larger
}

Pop: swap root with last, pop last, sift_down from 0.
All 5 tests in tests/minheap_test.rs must pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: MinHeap<T: Ord> with Vec<T> data field
sift_up: while i>0, parent=(i-1)/2, swap if data[i]<data[parent]
sift_down: find smallest child, swap if data[child]<data[i], repeat
pop swaps index 0 with last, pops, then sift_down(0)
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
